key_insight: Bidirectional cross-modal prompting lets event and frame modalities condition each other so their complementary strengths are preserved and aligned, yielding more reliable asymmetric stereo depth under fast motion and challenging illumination.
problem_solved: Asymmetric stereo using event and conventional frame cameras suffers from a modality gap that marginalizes one modality, causing poor correspondence and depth estimates in fast motion or low-light scenarios. This work closes that gap to improve stereo matching and disparity estimation.
method: Learned bidirectional prompts: generate and inject compact prompt tokens from events→frames and frames→events to condition encoder features and encourage mutual guidance.
Cross-modal attention & feature alignment: lightweight attention modules fuse temporal event cues with spatial frame detail, plus losses for disparity supervision and cross-modal consistency.
Temporal aggregation for events: accumulate event information into representations compatible with frame features to improve correspondence under motion and illumination changes.
impact: Enables robust 3D perception (depth/disparity) in robotics, autonomous driving, and AR by combining high-temporal-resolution event data with rich contextual frames, reducing motion blur and low-light failures. Makes integration of event cameras into stereo pipelines practical for real-world dynamic scenes.

paper_title: Bidirectional Cross-Modal Prompting for Event-Frame Asymmetric Stereo
paper_authors: Ninghui Xu, Fabio Tosi, Lihui Wang, Jiawei Han, Luca Bartolomei
